newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria raises fuel prices to stave off crisis.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria raises fuel prices to stave off crisis.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim government on Monday raised petrol prices by up to 178 percent in a bid to free suppliers' volumes kept in storage, prime minister Stefan Sofianski said.

"The new prices will be effective from Tuesday and it is high time that the fuel, which suppliers hold back, appeared on the (domestic) market. The fuel is held back," Sofianski told a news conference.
"We hope that the lev/dollar exchange rate will stabilise despite the price rise. The crisis and the chaos are enormous," he said.

On Friday the new interim government, which inherited crippling fuel and grain shortages, banned fuel exports until April 30 and troops enforced border controls in a bid to curb oil smuggling by companies and private motorists.
A litre of petrol cost 10 cents on Friday based on a rate of 660 levs per dollar. The lev traded around 3,000 per dollar on Friday.

As a result the country's biggest oil refinery Neftochim, which supplies almost the whole domestic market, has sunk into debts worth millions of dollars and suppliers have refused to deliver crude to it.

Most petrol stations have been closed because of the fuel shortage and municipalities are distributing petrol and diesel for ambulances, food delivery trucks, the police, the army and social services, officials said.
Production has been hit by cuts in bus services, transport officials said.

The refinery is distributing limited volumes of 680 tonnes of petrol and 680 tonnes of diesel per day. It has been refining up to 9,000 tonnes of crude per day since last Tuesday, while its daily capacity is 25,000.
Out of 650 buses 400 were running in Sofia on Monday due to fuel shortages, said Vassil Naidenov, chief of Sofia's public transport company.
Sofianski admitted that the drastic price rise would affect prices of all other goods. However, revised fuel prices were still not completely realistic, he added.
"We are trying to avoid blocking some sectors such as health care by extremely high prices," he said.

Neftochim has 68,000 tonnes of crude on stock after a 66,300-tonne tanker from the Bulgarian-Russian joint venture Rosbulneft supplied the refinery under its February contract for crude deliveries to the Bourgas refinery.
Sofianski said the cabinet relied on external funding and on sell-offs of Bulgarian plants to alleviate a cash shortage.

"If we manage to finalise the deal with Sodi Devnya by the end of the month, then the partial sale of the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company and eventually of Neftochim, things will get better," Sofianski told reporters later on Monday.
Belgian chemical group Solvay SA has said it had signed a preliminary agreement with Bulgaria's privatisation agency to acquire 60 percent of the major soda ash producer Sodi-Devnya for $160 million.
The interim cabinet may also increase a previously planned sale of 25 percent of the BTC to 51 percent, the local financial weekly Kapital quoted deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov as saying.
Sofianski announced on Friday plans for partial privatisation of the country's cash-stripped Neftochim refinery but gave no further details on Monday.
